Priya Kapoor: Heads up 3: I had to book a last-minute international flight for a customer emergency. Corporate travel site was down and the agency line had a 2hr wait, so I booked on my personal card. I also paid a "fare difference" to switch to a later flight and paid for a seat upgrade for medical comfort. What do you need to reimburse?
Sam Patel (Finance): Sorry to hear about the emergency. We can reimburse, but need specific docs.
Sam Patel (Finance): Required: screenshot of corporate travel outage (if available), original e-ticket/receipt from airline showing base fare and any change fees, the receipt showing the fare difference, proof of payment (card statement or screenshot), and a note from your manager approving the purchase (retro approvals are OK but discretionary).
Priya Kapoor: Manager note coming. Is the upgrade eligible? I paid for extra legroom + premium seat because my doctor recommended it for back issues. I have the medical note.
Maria (People Ops): Policy: seat upgrades for health reasons can be reimbursed if supported by a medical note and pre-approval. Since this was emergency and you have a doctor's note plus a manager sign-off, we can consider it eligible. Please redact any sensitive health details on the note and include only confirmation that extra seating was recommended.
Liam Chen (Manager): I approve retroactively. Priya had to respond immediately. Adding my note: "Approved - business necessity; emergency customer visit."
Sam Patel (Finance): Good. Also clarify: change/fare difference vs ticket refund. If you purchased a new ticket and didn't cancel the old refundable ticket, we need both receipts and an explanation. We only reimburse the net incremental business cost.
Priya Kapoor: Old ticket was fully refundable and I canceled it; refund is pending. I attached the refund confirmation email and the new ticket receipt.
travel-bot: Reminder: when refunds are pending, finance will hold reimbursement until refund is processed or will net the refund against the reimbursement. Upload refund_proof.pdf and new_ticket_receipt.pdf.
Sam Patel (Finance): For coding in Expensely:
```
Expense type: "Airfare - Emergency"
Project/Cost center: "Customer Success - EMEA"
GL account: "5100 - Travel"
Description: "Last-minute airfare due to customer emergency; fare difference and seat upgrade. Manager retro-approval attached."
Required attachments: airline_receipt.pdf, change_fee_receipt.pdf, proof_of_payment.pdf, manager_approval.pdf, doctor_note_redacted.pdf, refund_confirmation.pdf (if applicable)
```
Priya Kapoor: Quick Q on seat upgrade taxes/fees 1: the upgrade included a carrier-imposed surcharge and a VAT-like tax on the upgrade. Are taxes on upgrades reimbursable?
Sam Patel (Finance): Taxes and mandatory carrier surcharges that appear on the ticket are reimbursable. Optional add-ons (wi-fi, lounge access) are not reimbursable unless pre-approved or medically necessary. Document the line items on the airline receipt.
Maria (People Ops): Per-diem note: since Priya returned the same day, no overnight per-diem. If an overnight occurred because of rescheduling, per-diem would apply for overnight nights only and must be claimed separately.
Priya Kapoor: One more: the booking fee from my bank charged a foreign transaction fee. Is that reimbursable?
Sam Patel (Finance): Foreign transaction fees on personal cards are reimbursable when expense is business-related. Include the card statement line. For clarity, combine individual line items in one expense claim and attach all backups.
Priya Kapoor: Thanks. I'll file with all attachments. Anything else?
travel-bot: Tip: use "Attach as single claim" to avoid multiple reimbursements being split. Maximum 10MB per file. If docs are >10MB, split into multiple attachments and label them 1/2, 2/2.
Liam Chen (Manager): Thanks Priya for reacting quickly. Approved as described.
Priya Kapoor: Filing now. Appreciate the fast responses :heart:
